Subject: Follow-up: model fit & streaming quality (Acme Health)

Hi Jill & Carlos,

Thanks again for taking the time earlier — really helpful call. I wanted to capture the summary, our initial model recommendations, and the next steps so we can move the evals forward.

Quick summary from our side:
- Goals: integrate a streaming completion endpoint to support clinician-facing summarization and triage workflows; primary concerns are partial-output coherence during streaming, reliable stop sequences for multi-turn dialogs, and meeting latency SLOs for interactive use.
- Data: you indicated the content will be deidentified clinical notes for an initial POC (~100-200 samples).
- Compliance: Acme needs SOC2 evidence and an option to run on a private deployment if we move beyond POC.

Initial model fit / eval recommendations (high level):
- Recommend starting with two model families for A/B: "redwood-instruct-13b-quant" (fast, low-cost) and "redwood-rtl-70b-8bit" (higher quality for longer context).
- Run qualitative evals on your 100 deidentified prompts + our prompt-set (attached) and quantitative streaming benchmarks (attached CSV).
- Key metrics to capture: completion coherence (manual scoring), stop-sequence accuracy, partial-token stability (how often early streamed tokens change), median token latency, and overall per-response latency.

Streaming UX & quality notes:
- Partial output coherence is usually due to either decoding settings (temperature/top_p) or how the client handles incremental tokens. We suggest:
  - stricter stop sequences configured server-side (we can enforce token-level stop)
  - a short debounce/gap threshold on the client (e.g., 150-300ms) to reduce flicker for low-latency tokens
  - run evals with both greedy and top-p sampling to compare safety/accuracy tradeoffs
- For latency: our hosted endpoints can hit median token latencies in the 60-150ms range depending on model and context length; we'll include per-model medians in the attached benchmark CSV.

Attachments included: streaming-benchmarks-20260305.csv (benchmarks), prompt-set-acme-v1.txt (seed prompts), redwood-model-recommendations.pdf (short brief).

Next steps / asks:
1) Could you share the 100 deidentified sample prompts (CSV) so Dev can run a quick pass? (I see you have one — thanks in advance.)
2) Can we schedule a 30-min technical deep-dive with Dev & Nikhil next week to review the streaming setup and stop sequence config?
3) We'll provision a short-lived eval workspace and share links to run the A/B runs; aim to have initial results within 5 business days after we receive the samples.

Happy to adjust any of the above. Thank you — looking forward to the next steps.

Best,

Marissa — drafting some technical answers for Jill's Qs below. Feel free to paste into the reply.

--- draft ---
On stop-sequences:
- Streaming vs non-streaming: for streaming we perform token-level stop checks as tokens are emitted. That means as soon as the model emits a token that completes the configured stop sequence, the server will stop sending further tokens. This is stricter than client-side heuristics which might wait for a gap in the stream.
- Implementation note: we support multi-token stop sequences (e.g., "

## END
") and will return the final response with the stop tokens removed so the client receives a clean termination.

On latency SLOs (rough guidance):
- redwood-instruct-13b-quant: median token latency ~60-120ms; median full-response latency for typical 150-400 token replies ~200-800ms depending on batching and concurrency.
- redwood-rtl-70b-8bit: median token latency ~100-220ms; full-response latency ~400-1500ms for longer responses.
- Notes: these numbers assume our hosted Dedicated instance sizes that support 50 RPS with autoscaling and are measured at 95th percentile under balanced traffic. Quantization and batching configs can move you along the latency/cost curve.

Mitigations for partial coherence:
- Use deterministic decoding (lower temp) for clinician-facing outputs where exact phrasing matters.
- Keep prefix prompts compact and avoid re-sending large system context each request; use KV cache for long contexts where appropriate.

I'll run a couple quick passes against the attached sample prompts once we get the redacted CSV.

Cheers,
Dev
